messages.subject: Wallace v1.0.6 is on CRAN
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,

Wallace v1.0.6 is now on CRAN and Github (https://github.com/wallaceEcoMod/wallace).

NEWS
Wallace no longer needs rJava to run! Oh happy days! Wallace is now compatible with ENMeval 0.3.0, which now has no rJava dependency and runs Maxent using maxnet by default (CRAN package maxnet; https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1111/ecog.03049). This means Wallace no longer loads rJava automatically when using the ENMeval partition functions or running Maxent. You can still select the Java implementation of Maxent by choosing "maxent.jar" in the Maxent module, whereupon rJava will load.
- Wallace now works on computers that error when some non-ASCII characters are used. This problem was discovered during a workshop in Vietnam on some Chinese computers.
- Users can now select bioclimatic variables when using 30 arc second data.
- Added more instructions on how to troubleshoot installing rJava.
- Occurrence points with NA environmental values now disappear from the map.
- We also fixed some other small bugs dealing with the shiny code and Markdown file.
- MESS color gradient
- Small changes in text guidance

Best,
Wallace dev-team

messages.body_plain:
Dear Kerim,

I think that the component guidance in Wallace and the references are a good start point to answer this question. Unfortunately, there is not a unique "recipe" to choose the best model. The best model depends on your data and the question that you want to resolve.

Best,
Gonzalo

messages.subject: Re: Problem 8 Project
messages.body_plain:
Thanks for the notice. Wallace shouldn’t crash — it should tell you what the problem is instead, and we’ll look into that.

Are you using the Worldclim data downloaded through Wallace, or your own environmental data? If you use your own, you need to make sure that the rasters have an extent large enough for the projections you want to make. If you download through Wallace, you are getting the global dataset unless it is 30 arcsec (1 km) — in this case a single tile is downloaded (because of download limitations using the raster package) and you can only project to areas within that tile. If you are trying to project to other times, as we use the Worldclim database currently for all future climate scenarios, unfortunately it will only work with the bioclim layers.

Jamie Kass
PhD Candidate
City College of NY

I was wondering if it is possible to use both User Specified Environmental data and Worldclim 19 bioclimatic variables available on Wallace in one model, or if I need to manually upload the Worldclim rasters in addition to variables I am introducing. If I have to do it manually, why is the platform not reading the bill files? Is it because all the files have to be the same format or because Wallace can only read .tiff files?

Thank you in advanced, and I really appreciate and admire your work. Interactive platforms like this makes biologist's lives a lot easier!

Sincerely,

Paula Cardozo

messages.subject: Re: Environmental Data Upload
messages.body_plain:
Hi Paula,

Wallace just accepts user-rasters on TIFF or ASC files (more info in the module guidance). Also, you can not use both modules at the same time. I suggest getting all your rasters in one folder in the same format (TIF or ASC), resolution and extent. Then, upload to Wallace with the user-specified module.

Best,
Gonzalo

> Hello all,
> I am currently working on a species distribution model using both Worlclim bioclimatic variables (.bill files) and other specified environmental data (.tiff files). However, when I try to upload both file types it only recognizes the tiff and not the other 19 bioclimatic variables (.bill). I was wondering if it is possible to use both User Specified Environmental data and Worldclim 19 bioclimatic variables available on Wallace in one model, or if I need to manually upload the Worldclim rasters in addition to variables I am introducing. If I have to do it manually, why is the platform not reading the bill files? Is it because all the files have to be the same format or because Wallace can only read .tiff files?
>
> Thank you in advanced, and I really appreciate and admire your work. Interactive platforms like this makes biologist's lives a lot easier!
>
> Sincerely,
>
> Paula Cardozo
